name: Legacy cpuClass and oscpu
plain: Old non-standard strings naming the CPU class and operating system CPU.
meaning: cpuClass (old Internet Explorer) and oscpu (Firefox) mostly return nothing in Chrome, which is itself a signal for which browser engine runs.

fields.name: oscpu
fields.range: e.g. Intel Mac OS X 10.15 or undefined

limits.headline: Can sometimes see an old CPU and OS string, mostly in Firefox
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a page checks the old browser fields
can: Get the oscpu text in Firefox
Notice when Chrome returns nothing, which hints at the engine
Use the answer to guess the browser and OS
cannot: See anything useful in Chrome, Safari, or Edge
See your exact chip or speed
Get the old cpuClass value outside very old Internet Explorer
Learn your name or location from it
limits.differs: Only Firefox returns the oscpu value. Chrome, Safari, and Edge return nothing.

story.what_it_is: Old strings that name your processor and system, mostly empty now, which itself hints at your browser.
story.for_you: You never see these. Most return nothing. The fact that one is empty and another is filled in is what reveals which browser engine you use.
story.for_makers: These came from the 1990s and 2000s browser wars. Today they are mostly a consistency test: a bot that pretends to be Firefox but returns the wrong answer gets caught. They add a few bits to a device profile.

use_cases.example: A bot defence service tests whether Firefox-only strings exist when a visitor claims to be Firefox, and challenges those that fail.
An old analytics script still reads the strings to label visitors by browser family.
An ad fraud vendor checks that the strings match the claimed browser before counting an ad view as real.
A compatibility test page prints these values to show what an unusual browser reports.
A browser games portal uses them to hide a feature in browsers that never supported it.
A bank's login risk engine adds a point when old strings and the user agent disagree.

risks: Mismatch can wrongly flag a person
